item.research_question: How does varying the Cr content (x = 0 to 1) affect the microstructure, hardness, high-temperature oxidation resistance, and corrosion resistance of WVTaTiCr x refractory high-entropy alloy coatings prepared by laser cladding?
item.material_system: WVTaTiCr x (x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1) refractory high-entropy alloy coatings on 42-CrMo steel substrate
item.processing_route: Laser cladding using a LYHS series ultra-high-speed laser-cladding machine; powder mixture of W, V, Ta, Ti, Cr (45–105 μm, 99.9% purity) ball-milled for 24 h at 300 r/min (10:1 ball-to-material ratio); laser power 1.4 kW, scanning speed 8 mm/s, spot diameter 6 mm, overlap rate 30–40%, argon protective gas
item.test_conditions: Microhardness tested at 1.96 N load for 15 s; high-temperature oxidation at 800 °C for 50 h with heating rate 5 °C/min and air cooling every 10 h; corrosion testing in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution using potentiostat with Tafel analysis
key_findings: The average hardness of the WVTaTiCr (Cr 1) alloy coating reaches 627.36 HV, significantly higher than the substrate.
After 50 h of high-temperature oxidation at 800 °C, the oxide weight of WVTaTiCr (Cr 1) increases by 5.12 mg/cm², with an oxidation rate of 0.10 mg/(cm²·h).
In 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, the corrosion potential of WVTaTiCr (Cr 1) is −0.3198 V, and the corrosion rate is 0.161 mm/a.
The addition of Cr promotes the precipitation of the Laves phase (Cr₂Ta), which forms a network distribution within the dendritic region.
With increasing Cr content, the coating grains are refined, and the dendritic structure becomes more uniform.
The WVTaTi (Cr 0) coating has a corrosion potential of −0.7783 V and a corrosion rate of 2.959 mm/a, whereas Cr 1 shows superior corrosion resistance.
The main phase in all coatings is the BCC solid-solution phase, with no other complex intermetallic compounds observed.
item.mechanism: The addition of Cr causes more severe lattice distortion, opening a path for atomic diffusion and promoting the precipitation of the Laves phase (Cr₂Ta) due to the strong binding ability between Cr and Ta (enthalpy of mixing −7 KJ/mol). The dense oxide film formed by CrTaO₄, TiO₂, and Cr₂O₃ inhibits oxygen diffusion, reducing the oxidation rate. Additionally, Cr promotes the generation of a denser and more uniform passive film, reducing ion diffusion in NaCl solution and improving corrosion resistance.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The improved mechanical and oxidation properties of WVTaTiCr indicate the potential for future use in fusion applications.
